translation_en: Said ibn Mansur narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Hani al-Khawlani narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abu Said al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah said: Abu Said, whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as prophet, Paradise is assured for him. Abu Said was amazed by this, so he said: Messenger of Allah, repeat it to me. He did so, then said: And there is another deed by which a servant is raised one hundred ranks in Paradise, the distance between each two ranks being like the distance between heaven and earth. Abu Said asked: What is it, Messenger of Allah? He said: Striving in the cause of Allah, striving in the cause of Allah.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Said ibn Abi Said, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who heard the Messenger of Allah stand among them and say: Striving in the cause of Allah and belief in Allah are the best deeds. A man stood up and asked: Messenger of Allah, if I am killed in Allah's cause, will my sins be expiated? The Messenger of Allah said: Yes, if you are killed in Allah's cause while patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating. Then the Messenger of Allah asked: What did you say? He replied: If I am killed in Allah's cause, will my sins be expiated? The Messenger of Allah said: Yes, while you are patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating—except debt, for Gabriel told me that.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Yahya (Ibn Said) informed us, from Said ibn Abi Said al-Maqburi, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah and asked: What if I am killed in Allah's cause? He reported a hadith with the meaning of Layth's narration.

Said ibn Mansur narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Muhammad ibn Qays. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Ajlan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, from the Prophet. One of the two adds that a man came to the Prophet while he was on the pulpit and asked: What if I strike with my sword? This is with the meaning of al-Maqburi's hadith.

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Salih al-Misri narrated to us: al-Mufaddal (Ibn Fadalah) narrated to us, from Ayyash (Ibn Abbas al-Qitbani), from Abdullah ibn Yazid Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Messenger of Allah said: The martyr is forgiven every sin except debt.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us: Said ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us: Ayyash ibn Abbas al-Qitbani narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Prophet said: Being killed in Allah's cause atones for everything except debt.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah both report from Abu Muawiyah. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Jarir and Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, all from al-Amash. [Another chain, in this wording:] Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Asbat and Abu Muawiyah narrated to us: al-Amash narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: We asked Abdullah about this verse: 'Do not think that those who are killed in Allah's cause are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.' (Quran 3:169) He said: We asked about that, and he said: Their souls are inside green birds with lamps suspended from the Throne. They roam wherever they wish in Paradise, then return to those lamps. Their Lord looked upon them and said: Do you desire anything? They said: What could we desire when we roam wherever we wish in Paradise? He did that with them three times. When they saw that they would continue to be asked, they said: Our Lord, we wish You would return our souls to our bodies so that we could be killed in Your cause once again. When He saw that they had no further request, they were left in peace.

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, from Ata ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Said al-Khudri, that a man came to the Prophet and asked: Who is the best of people? He said: A man who strives in Allah's cause with his wealth and his life. The man asked: Then who? He said: A believer in one of the mountain passes, worshipping his Lord and keeping people safe from his own harm.

Abd ibn Humayd informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ata ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Said, who said: A man asked: Messenger of Allah, who is the best of people? He said: A believer who strives in Allah's cause with his life and wealth. The man asked: Then who? He said: Then a man who withdraws to a mountain pass, worships his Lord, and keeps people safe from his own harm.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, from al-Awzai, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain. He said: 'And a man in a mountain pass,' but did not say: 'Then a man.'

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, from his father, from Bajah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Among the best ways people can live is for a man to hold the reins of his horse in Allah's cause, flying upon its back. Whenever he hears an alarm or a cry of fear, he mounts it and seeks death wherever it may be found. Or, a man with a small flock on the summit of one of these mountain peaks or in one of these valleys, establishing prayer, paying zakat, and worshipping his Lord until certainty (death) comes to him, harming no one and doing nothing but good.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated this to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim and Yaqoub (Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qari), both from Abu Hazim, with this chain and a similar report. He said: Bajah ibn Abdullah ibn Badr. He also said: 'in one of these mountain passes,' differing from Yahya's narration.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Abu Kurayb said: Waki narrated to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from Bajah ibn Abdullah al-Juhani, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with the meaning of Abu Hazim's hadith from Bajah. He said: 'in one of the mountain passes.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: Allah smiles at two men, one of whom kills the other, yet both enter Paradise. They asked: How is that, Messenger of Allah? He said: One fights in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and is martyred. Then Allah accepts the killer's repentance, he becomes Muslim, fights in Allah's cause, and is martyred.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Abu Kurayb said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zinad, with this chain and a similar report.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. He mentioned several hadiths, including that the Messenger of Allah said: Allah smiles at two men, one of whom kills the other, yet both enter Paradise. They asked: How is that, Messenger of Allah? He said: This man is killed and enters Paradise; then Allah accepts the other's repentance and guides him to Islam, after which he strives in Allah's cause and is martyred.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ali ibn Hujr said: Ismail (Ibn Jafar) narrated to us, from al-Ala, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: An unbeliever and the one who killed him will never be together in the Fire.

Abdullah ibn Awn al-Hilali narrated to us: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: They will not both be together in the Fire in a way that harms one of them. It was asked: Who are they, Messenger of Allah? He said: A believer who killed an unbeliever, then remained upright.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali informed us: Jarir informed us, from al-Amash, from Abu Amr al-Shaybani, from Abu Masud al-Ansari, who said: A man came with a camel whose nose was tied by a rope and said: This is in Allah's cause. The Messenger of Allah said: For it, you will have seven hundred camels on the Day of Resurrection, each with its nose tied by a rope.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Za'idah. [Another chain:] Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad (Ibn Jafar) narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us. Both report from al-Amash with this chain.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us; the wording is Abu Kurayb's. They said: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abu Amr al-Shaybani, from Abu Masud al-Ansari, who said: A man came to the Prophet and said: My mount has become exhausted; provide me with a mount. He said: I have none. Another man said: Messenger of Allah, I can direct him to someone who can provide him with a mount. The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever directs someone to good will have a reward like the one who does it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us. [Another chain:] Bishr ibn Khalid informed me: Muhammad ibn Jafar informed us, from Shubah. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Sufyan informed us. All report from al-Amash with this chain.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik. [Another chain, in this wording:] Abu Bakr ibn Nafi narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, that a young man from Aslam said: Messenger of Allah, I want to go on an expedition, but I have nothing with which to equip myself. He said: Go to so-and-so, for he had equipped himself but became ill. The young man went to him and said: The Messenger of Allah sends you greetings and asks you to give me what you prepared for the expedition. The man said: So-and-so, give him what I prepared, and do not hold anything back from him. By Allah, do not withhold anything, so that it may be blessed for you.

Said ibn Mansur and Abu al-Tahir narrated to us. Abu al-Tahir said: Ibn Wahb informed us; Said said: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Busr ibn Said, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Whoever equips a fighter in Allah's cause has himself fought, and whoever looks after a fighter's family well has himself fought.

Abu al-Rabi al-Zahrani narrated to us: Yazid (Ibn Zuray) narrated to us: Husayn al-Muallim narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Busr ibn Said, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: The Prophet of Allah said: Whoever equips a fighter has himself fought, and whoever looks after a fighter's family has himself fought.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ismail (Ibn Ulayyah) narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Mubarak: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us: Abu Said, the freedman of al-Mahri, narrated to me, from Abu Said al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah sent a detachment to Banu Lihyan, from Hudhayl, and said: Let one of every two men set out, and the reward will be shared between them.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated this to me: Abd al-Samad (Ibn Abd al-Warith) informed us, who said: I heard my father narrate: Husayn narrated to us, from Yahya, who said: Abu Said, the freedman of al-Mahri, narrated to me: Abu Said al-Khudri narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah sent out a detachment, with the same meaning. Ishaq ibn Mansur also said: Ubaydullah (Ibn Musa) informed us, from Shayban, from Yahya, with the same chain and a similar report.

Said ibn Mansur narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Yazid ibn Abi Said, the freedman of al-Mahri, from his father, from Abu Said al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah sent men to Banu Lihyan and said: Let one man go out from every two. Then he said to the one who stayed behind: If any of you looks after the one who went out's family and property well, he will have half the reward of the one who went out.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: The inviolability of the wives of those striving in Allah's cause is like that of their mothers for those who stay behind. Any man among those who stay behind, entrusted with the family of a man striving in Allah's cause, who betrays him in regard to them will be made to stand before him on the Day of Resurrection, and the latter may take whatever he wishes from the former's good deeds. What do you think of that?

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Misar narrated to us, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said that the Prophet said something with the meaning of al-Thawri's hadith.
